GRADE 9 MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Time: 96 minutes

INSTRUCTIONS
1. This is an advanced revision paper.
2. Show working where needed.
3. Answer all questions.
2. For multiple choice, write the correct letter only.
3. For short answers, write clearly in the spaces provided.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A: Multiple Choice

1. About Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. perform basic operations on Integers in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers completely.
   C. Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers.

2. About Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. work out combined operations on Integers in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers completely.
   C. Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers.

3. About Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. apply Integers to real- life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers completely.
   C. Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Integers Simple and combined operations on Integers.

5. About Cubes and Cube Roots at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. work out cubes of numbers by multiplication in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Cubes and Cube Roots completely.
   C. Cubes and Cube Roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Cubes and Cube Roots.

6. About Cubes and Cube Roots using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. determine cubes of numbers from mathematical tables in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Cubes and Cube Roots completely.
   C. Cubes and Cube Roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Cubes and Cube Roots.

7. About Cubes and Cube Roots when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. determine cube roots of numbers by factor method in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Cubes and Cube Roots completely.
   C. Cubes and Cube Roots is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Cubes and Cube Roots.

9. About Indices and Logarithms at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. express numbers in index form in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Indices and Logarithms completely.
   C. Indices and Logarithms is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Indices and Logarithms.

10. About Indices and Logarithms using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. generate the laws of Indices in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Indices and Logarithms completely.
   C. Indices and Logarithms is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Indices and Logarithms.

   A. apply the laws of indices in different situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Indices and Logarithms completely.
   C. Indices and Logarithms is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Indices and Logarithms.

13. About Compound Proportions and Rates of Work at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. divide quantities into proportional parts in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Compound Proportions and Rates of Work completely.
   C. Compound Proportions and Rates of Work is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Compound Proportions and Rates of Work.

14. About Compound Proportions and Rates of Work using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. relate different proportional parts in real-life situations,
   B. Learners should ignore Compound Proportions and Rates of Work completely.

15. About Compound Proportions and Rates of Work when counting items at home, which statement is correct?

17. About Matrices at the market in your county, which statement is correct?

   B. Learners should ignore Matrices completely.
   C. Matrices is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Matrices.

19. About Matrices when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. determine the position of items in a matrix in different situations.
   B. Learners should ignore Matrices completely.
   C. Matrices is only useful outside Kenya.

21. About Equations of Straight Lines at the market in your county, which statement is correct?

26. About Linear Inequalities using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?

   B. Learners should ignore Linear Inequalities completely.

   D. There is no need to practise Linear Inequalities.

27. About Linear Inequalities when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. represent linear inequality in two unknowns graphically.
   B. Learners should ignore Linear Inequalities completely.
   C. Linear Inequalities is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Linear Inequalities.

29. About Area at the market in your county, which statement is correct?

   B. Learners should ignore Area completely.
   C. Area is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Area.

30. About Area using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the surface area of triangular and rectangular-based prisms.
   B. Learners should ignore Area completely.
   C. Area is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Area.

31. About Area when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the surface area of triangular, rectangular, and square-based pyramids.
   B. Learners should ignore Area completely.
   C. Area is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Area.

33. About Volume of Solids at the market in your county, which statement is correct?
   A. work out the volume of triangular and rectangular-based prisms.
   B. Learners should ignore Volume of Solids completely.
   C. Volume of Solids is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Volume of Solids.

   C. Volume of Solids is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Volume of Solids.

37. About Mass, Volume, Weight and Density at the market in your county, which statement is correct?

   B. Learners should ignore Mass, Volume, Weight and Density completely.
   C. Mass, Volume, Weight and Density is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Mass, Volume, Weight and Density.

38. About Mass, Volume, Weight and Density using objects in your classroom, which statement is correct?
   A. relate mass and weight in real-life situations.
   B. Learners should ignore Mass, Volume, Weight and Density completely.
   C. Mass, Volume, Weight and Density is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Mass, Volume, Weight and Density.

39. About Mass, Volume, Weight and Density when counting items at home, which statement is correct?
   A. determine mass, volume, and density of different substances,
   B. Learners should ignore Mass, Volume, Weight and Density completely.
   C. Mass, Volume, Weight and Density is only useful outside Kenya.
   D. There is no need to practise Mass, Volume, Weight and Density.
